# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, -the CLI tree, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they -cannot drift from it. +and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from +it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. +### When something fails + +Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every +HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — +`{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — +and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your +question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the +canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when +the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the +`request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and +on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. + ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity -agentic-odi framework-guidelines # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide -agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can help with agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page. The artwork is original, generated by a committed script, and documented in [brand/README.md](brand/README.md). ```bash uv run python brand/tools/render.py # regenerate every Odi asset ``` ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---

     if value:
         if ctx.params.get("verbose"):
             typer.echo(version.verbose_summary())
         else:

         raise typer.Exit()
 
 
 def _startup_auto_update(no_update: bool) -> None:
     """Best-effort background auto-update; never raises, never blocks."""
     try:
         updated = update.maybe_auto_update(no_update=no_update, now=time.time())
         if updated is not None:
             typer.echo(f"Updated to v{updated} — takes effect next run")
     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
         return None
 
 
 @app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)
 def main(
     ctx: typer.Context,
     version: bool = typer.Option(
         False, "--version", callback=_version_callback, help="Show version"
     ),
     verbose: bool = typer.Option(

         "--verbose",
         is_eager=True,
         help="Show verbose version information (with --version)",
     ),

 ) -> None:  # noqa: B008
     context.set_options(backend=backend, db_path=db, mcp_url=mcp_url)
     if not no_update:
         threading.Thread(target=_startup_auto_update, args=(no_update,), daemon=True).start()
 
     if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:

 def _reexec_current() -> None:
     """Re-exec into the freshly installed binary (POSIX only)."""
     current = paths.current_link()
     binary = current / "odi"
     can_exec = (
         os.name == "posix" and hasattr(os, "execv") and current.is_symlink() and binary.exists()

 ) -> None:

     if check:
         latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
         if latest is None:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
         return

         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
         return
 
     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
     if target is None:
         if force:
             target = __version__
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
             return

             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())

 def _apply_add_connector(
     arguments: dict[str, Any], service: ConnectorService
 ) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
     """Register a connector locally and return SSE event dicts for the stream."""
     name = arguments.get("name")
     preset_id = arguments.get("preset")
     url = arguments.get("url")
     try:
         config = service.add(name=name, preset_id=preset_id, url=url)
     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
         event = {"event": "connector", "data": {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}}
         return f"Error: {exc}", [event]
     event_data: dict[str, Any] = {"action": "registered", "name": config.name}
     if preset_id is not None:
         event_data["preset"] = preset_id
     if url is not None:
         event_data["url"] = url
     return f"registered connector {config.name}", [{"event": "connector", "data": event_data}]
 
 
 def _apply_remember(
     arguments: dict[str, Any], memory: StudioMemory | None
 ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
     """Store one suggested observation without asking the PM first."""
     if memory is None:
         return "Memory is not available to this client.", None
 
     kind = str(arguments.get("kind", ""))
     text = str(arguments.get("text", ""))
     data = arguments.get("data")
     try:
         confidence = float(arguments.get("confidence", 0.6))
     except (TypeError, ValueError):
         confidence = 0.6
 
     try:
         observation = memory.add_observation(
             kind=kind,
             text=text,
             data=data if isinstance(data, dict) else None,
             status="suggested",
             confidence=confidence,
         )
     except ValueError as exc:
         return f"Could not remember that: {exc}", None
     return "Saved for the user to review.", {"observation": observation.to_dict()}

+    """Yield SSE frames: status, conversation, delta, tool, ui, memory, connector, message, error.
+
+    Every turn ends with exactly one terminal event: one ``message`` or one
+    ``error``. A failure is never dressed up as a success, and it never leaves
+    the stream without an ending.
+    """
+    rid = request_id or ""
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    counters = {"rounds": 0, "tool_calls": 0, "tool_errors": 0, "rounds_exhausted": 0}
+    outcome = "failed"
+    error_code: str | None = None
+    try:
+        async for chunk in _turn_frames(request, service, memory, rid, counters):
+            yield chunk
+        outcome = "completed"
+        if counters["tool_errors"]:
+            outcome = "partial"
+        if counters["rounds_exhausted"]:
+            outcome = "rounds_exhausted"
+    except _TurnFailure as failure:
+        yield _error_frame(failure.error, rid)
+        outcome = "failed"
+        error_code = failure.error.code.value
+    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+        log.exception("chat turn failed (request_id=%s)", rid)
+        yield _error_frame(
+            StudioError(
+                code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
+                message="The turn failed unexpectedly.",
+                suggestion="Try again — your question is still here.",
+            ),
+            rid,
+        )
+        outcome = "failed"
+    finally:
+        log_turn(
+            request_id=rid,
+            model=request.model,
+            rounds=counters["rounds"],
+            tool_calls=counters["tool_calls"],
+            tool_errors=counters["tool_errors"],

+"""HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.
+
+Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::
+
+    {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
+               "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}
+
+The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
+sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import re
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
+from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
+from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"
+
+#: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
+#: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
+REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")
+
+STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
+    StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
+    StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
+    StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
+    StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
+    StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
+    StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
+    StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
+    StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
+    StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
+}
+
+CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
+    400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
+    404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
+    409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
+    422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
+    500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
+    502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
+}
+
+
+class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
+    """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""
+
+    def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
+        self.error = error
+        self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
+        super().__init__(error.message)
+
+
+def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
+    """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
+    return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)
+
+
+def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:
+    """Return the error code that belongs to an HTTP status."""
+    return CODE_FOR_STATUS.get(status_code, StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL)
+
+
+def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
+    """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
+    return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")
+
+
+def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    request_id = request_id_for(request)
+    if not error.request_id:
+        error = error.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id})
+    return {"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}
+
+
+def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
+    request_id = request_id_for(request)
+    headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
+    return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)
+
+
+def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:
+    """Render a :class:`StudioHTTPError` as the one error body."""
+    return _error_response(request, exc.error, exc.status_code)
+
+
+def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
+    """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
+    detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
+    error = StudioError(
+        code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
+        message="Request validation failed.",
+        detail=detail,
+        suggestion="Check the request body and try again.",
+    )
+    return _error_response(request, error, 422)
+
+
+def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    for error in exc.errors():
+        location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
+        parts.append(f"{location}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
+    return "; ".join(parts)
+
+
+def http_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
+    """Render a Starlette/FastAPI ``HTTPException`` as the one error body."""
+    error = StudioError(
+        code=code_for_status(exc.status_code),
+        message=str(exc.detail),
+    )
+    return _error_response(request, error, exc.status_code)
+
+
+def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
+    """Log an unexpected failure and return it without internals."""
+    request_id = request_id_for(request)
+    logger.exception("unhandled studio-api error (request_id=%s)", request_id, exc_info=exc)
+    error = StudioError(
+        code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
+        message="Something went wrong. The team has been notified.",
+    )
+    return _error_response(request, error, 500)
+
+
+def _safe_request_id(candidate: str | None) -> str:
+    """Return the client's request id when it is safe to echo, else a fresh one."""
+    if candidate and REQUEST_ID_PATTERN.match(candidate):
+        return candidate
+    return uuid4().hex
+
+
+class RequestIdMiddleware:
+    """Accept or mint an ``X-Request-ID`` and echo it on the response."""
+
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        request_id = _safe_request_id(Headers(scope=scope).get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER))
+        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
+
+        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                MutableHeaders(scope=message)[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = request_id
+            await send(message)
+
+        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
+
+
+def register_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
+    """Install the one-error-body handlers on an app."""
+    handler: Any = studio_error_handler
+    app.add_exception_handler(StudioHTTPError, handler)
+    handler = validation_error_handler
+    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, handler)
+    handler = http_error_handler
+    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, handler)
+    handler = unhandled_error_handler
+    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, handler)

+"""Per-turn observability: one structured log line, with redaction.
+
+The turn log is what makes a failure diagnosable after the fact, so it must
+carry the request id, the shape of the turn, and how it ended — and nothing
+that could leak a token, an API key, or a customer's words.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+REDACTED = "[redacted]"
+
+#: Keys whose values must never reach a log line.
+SENSITIVE_KEYS = frozenset(
+    {
+        "api_key",
+        "apikey",
+        "authorization",
+        "password",
+        "secret",
+        "token",
+        "access_token",
+        "refresh_token",
+        "quote",
+        "quotes",
+        "transcript",
+        "customer_words",
+    }
+)
+
+
+def _is_sensitive(key: str) -> bool:
+    lowered = key.lower()
+    if lowered in SENSITIVE_KEYS:
+        return True
+    return any(marker in lowered for marker in ("token", "secret", "password", "api_key"))
+
+
+def redact(mapping: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return a copy of ``mapping`` with sensitive values replaced."""
+    return {key: REDACTED if _is_sensitive(str(key)) else value for key, value in mapping.items()}
+
+
+def log_turn(**fields: Any) -> None:
+    """Write one JSON log line describing a chat turn.
+
+    Sensitive fields are dropped outright: the line says what happened in the
+    turn, and it must not name a secret any more than it carries its value.
+    Nested mappings are redacted rather than dropped, so a context that is
+    worth keeping can still be logged.
+    """
+    payload: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for key, value in fields.items():
+        if _is_sensitive(str(key)):
+            continue
+        payload[key] = redact(value) if isinstance(value, Mapping) else value
+    log.info(json.dumps(payload, default=str, sort_keys=True))

+

+

+    body = response.json()
+    assert body["error"]["code"] == "internal"

 # Data Flow
 
 ## Sources of Truth
 
 | Layer | Owns | Persists |
 |---|---|---|
 | `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
 | `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
 | `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop, conversation history, PM memory | Via the same repository when the local backend is active; conversations and memory in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
 | `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
 | `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |
 
 ## Write Paths
 
 ### Local CLI
 
 ```text
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
   -> LocalBackend
   -> ODIService
   -> SQLiteRepository
   -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
 ```
 
 ### MCP
 
 ```text
 MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
   -> FastMCP tool
   -> ODIService
   -> configured Repository
 ```
 
 `apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).
 
 ### Studio API
 
 ```text
 apps/studio SPA
   -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
   -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
   -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository
 
 apps/studio SPA
   -> /api/chat
   -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
   -> StudioMemory (conversation turns + remembered observations)
 ```
 
 The studio memory is a separate SQLite file, not an ODI repository. It never
 feeds the canvas; it only supplies bounded context to the next chat turn.
 
 The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.
 
 ## Read Paths
 
 ```text
 ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
   -> Repository read-through state
   -> Pydantic models
   -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
 ```
 
 The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.
 
 ## Configuration
 
 | Variable | Used by | Default |
 |---|---|---|
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` | Studio API memory | `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |
 
 ## Trust Boundaries
 
 - The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
 - The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
 - MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.
+
+## The Failure Path
+
+A failure is a first-class result, not an empty success. The path is the same
+for the CLI, the sidecar, and the SPA.
+
+```text
+MCP tool result (text)
+  -> agentic_odi_core.remote.parse_tool_result
+  -> StudioError { code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id }
+  -> sidecar: StudioHTTPError -> HTTP status + {"error": StudioError}
+  -> SPA: StudioApiError -> FailurePanel (message, detail, suggestion, Retry)
+```
+
+- **One error body.** Every HTTP failure is `{"error": StudioError}`. The SPA
+  also reads a legacy `{"detail": "..."}` body, so an older sidecar still
+  produces a readable message. Write routes no longer wrap their result in
+  `{"ok": true, "result": ...}`: a success is the object, a delete is
+  `{"deleted": id}`.
+- **One terminal chat event.** Every `/api/chat` stream ends with exactly one
+  `message` or one `error`. A recoverable tool error stays a tool result the
+  model can read, but it is reported as `status: "error"` and counted. A fatal
+  failure ends the stream with `event: error` carrying the `StudioError`.
+- **Request ids.** The sidecar accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on
+  the response, and puts it on every SSE frame. The MCP server's own log line
+  and the `Execution` record (#82) do not carry it yet, and authentication
+  (#90) is out of scope.
+- **The canvas is a union.** `CanvasState` is `loading | ready | empty |
+  error`. An empty canvas is an invitation; a failed canvas is a failure panel
+  with Retry. The two never look the same.
+- **The turn log is safe.** One JSON line per turn carries the request id, the
+  model, the round and tool counts, the error count, the duration, and the
+  outcome. Sensitive keys are dropped rather than redacted, so no token, key,
+  or customer quote can reach the log.
+

 # CLI Reference
 
 The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
 command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
 provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
 commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
 required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
 
 Install the workspace first if you have not already:
 
 ```bash
 uv sync --all-packages
 ```
 
 ## Launching
 
 ```bash
 python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
 python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
 python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
 ```
 
 A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
 
 ## Global options
 
 | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
 | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
 | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
 
 Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
 machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
 (`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
 
 ## Interactive chat
 
 `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
 offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
 MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
 and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.
 
 ```bash
 agentic-odi chat
 agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
 ```
 
 ### Connection settings
 
 The chat resolves settings in priority order:
 **CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**
 
 | Variable | Default | CLI flag |
 |---|---|---|
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
 
 The **persisted profile** is stored at
 `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
 within the session using `/connect`.
 
 ### Slash commands
 
 | Command | Description |
 |---|---|
 | `/help` | Show all available commands |
 | `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
 | `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
 | `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
 | `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
 | `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
 | `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
 | `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |
 
 ### /connect wizard
 
 `/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:
 
 1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
 2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
 3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
 4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
 5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
 6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions
 
 The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
 > and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
 
 ## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes
 
 Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
 the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
 Job cascades to both.
 
 ```bash
 # Jobs
 agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
 agentic-odi jobs list
 agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
 agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
 agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
 
 # Steps (Job Map)
 agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
 agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
 agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
 agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
 
 # Desired Outcomes
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 ```
 
 Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.
 
 ## Evidence
 
 Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
 a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
 artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.
 
 ```bash
 # Capture a record by hand
 agentic-odi evidence add \
   --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
   --name "Support lead" \
   --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
   --job-id <job-id>
 
 # Read and delete
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
 agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
 agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
 
 # Promote into the ODI model
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
 ```
 
 `connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
 ingested batch into evidence in one step.
 
 ## Schema and scoring
 
 ```bash
-agentic-odi schema                   # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
-agentic-odi framework-guidelines     # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide
-agentic-odi capabilities             # what the assistant can help with
-agentic-odi score 8 2                # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
 ```
 
 ## Manage Customer Outcomes
 
 Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
 writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
 to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
 available under its historical name `outcomes`.
 
 ```bash
 # Add a Customer Outcome
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
   --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
 
 # Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
   --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
 
 # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
 
 # Get, update, delete
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

 agentic-odi score 8 2
 agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
 ```
 
 `score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
 `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
 
 Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
 using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 
 ## Connectors
 
 The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
 [External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
 ingest behavior.
 
 ```bash
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
 ```
 
 ## Updates
 
 `odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
 default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
 `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+"""Pause acting tool calls until the person using the studio has agreed.
+
+The agent reads freely, but anything that changes the PM's workspace is a
+proposal first. :class:`ConsentGate` keeps that rule in one place: a call is
+requested, the person approves or declines it, and only then may it run.
+Read-only tools pass straight through and never need a gate.
+
+The acting set is derived from :class:`~agentic_odi_core.contract.ToolName`, so
+a tool added to the contract is treated as acting until someone classifies it
+as read-only.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, TypeVar
+
+from agentic_odi_core.contract import ToolName
+from agentic_odi_core.errors import ConsentRequired
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+READ_ONLY_TOOLS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
+    {
+        ToolName.GET_JOBS.value,
+        ToolName.GET_JOB.value,
+        ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value,
+        ToolName.GET_STEP.value,
+        ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value,
+        ToolName.GET_OUTCOME.value,
+        ToolName.GET_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME.value,
+        ToolName.LIST_CUSTOMER_OUTCOMES.value,
+        ToolName.GET_EVIDENCE.value,
+        ToolName.LIST_EVIDENCE.value,
+        ToolName.EVALUATE_OUTCOME.value,
+        ToolName.GET_ODI_SCHEMA.value,
+        ToolName.COMPUTE_OPPORTUNITY.value,
+        ToolName.GET_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES.value,
+        ToolName.GET_CAPABILITIES.value,
+    }
+)
+
+ACTING_TOOLS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(name.value for name in ToolName) - READ_ONLY_TOOLS
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Proposal:
+    """An acting tool call waiting for the PM's decision."""
+
+    id: int
+    tool: str
+    arguments: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class ConsentGate:
+    """Hold acting calls until they are approved, one proposal at a time."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._pending: dict[int, Proposal] = {}
+        self._approved: set[int] = set()
+        self._next_id = 1
+
+    def request(self, tool: str, arguments: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Proposal:
+        """Queue an acting call. Nothing is executed here."""
+        if tool not in ACTING_TOOLS:
+            raise ValueError(f"{tool} is read-only and does not need consent")
+        proposal = Proposal(id=self._next_id, tool=tool, arguments=dict(arguments or {}))
+        self._next_id += 1
+        self._pending[proposal.id] = proposal
+        return proposal
+
+    def pending(self) -> list[Proposal]:
+        return list(self._pending.values())
+
+    def approve(self, proposal: Proposal) -> None:
+        if self._pending.pop(proposal.id, None) is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"proposal {proposal.id} is not waiting for consent")
+        self._approved.add(proposal.id)
+
+    def decline(self, proposal: Proposal) -> bool:
+        """Drop a pending proposal. Returns whether it was still waiting."""
+        return self._pending.pop(proposal.id, None) is not None
+
+    def execute(self, proposal: Proposal, action: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], T]) -> T:
+        """Run an approved acting call exactly once."""
+        if proposal.id in self._pending:
+            raise ConsentRequired(
+                f"{proposal.tool} is waiting for consent; approve or decline it first"
+            )
+        if proposal.id not in self._approved:
+            raise ValueError(f"proposal {proposal.id} is not waiting for consent")
+        self._approved.discard(proposal.id)
+        return action(proposal.arguments)

 """Error types for Agentic ODI operations.
 
 Every failure mode in the domain has a dedicated exception class so callers
 can branch on the *kind* of failure instead of matching on message text. All
 ODI errors inherit from :class:`OdiError`, so a single ``except OdiError``
 catches anything this package raises deliberately.
 
 Note that :class:`ValidationError` here is the *ODI contract* error. Pydantic's
 own ``ValidationError`` remains available from ``pydantic`` and is unrelated.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 
 class OdiError(Exception):
     """Base class for every deliberate Agentic ODI failure."""
 
 
 class ValidationError(OdiError, ValueError):
     """Input did not satisfy the ODI contract.
 
     Also a :class:`ValueError` so that callers written against the previous
     behaviour (which raised bare ``ValueError``) keep working unchanged.
     """
 
 
 class NotFoundError(OdiError):
-    """A referenced resource does not exist."""
+    """A referenced resource does not exist.
 
-    def __init__(self, resource_id: str, kind: str) -> None:
+    ``hint`` is an optional sentence telling the caller what to do next. It is
+    appended to the message so it survives into user-facing output.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, resource_id: str, kind: str, hint: str | None = None) -> None:
         self.resource_id = resource_id
         self.kind = kind
-        super().__init__(f"{kind} not found: {resource_id}")
+        self.hint = hint or ""
+        message = f"{kind} not found: {resource_id}"
+        if self.hint:
+            message = f"{message}. {self.hint}"
+        super().__init__(message)
 
 
 class ConflictError(OdiError):
     """The requested change conflicts with the current state."""
 
 
 class RateLimitError(OdiError):
     """The caller exceeded an allowed rate or volume."""
 
     def __init__(
         self, message: str = "Rate limit exceeded", retry_after: float | None = None
     ) -> None:
         self.retry_after = retry_after
         super().__init__(message)
 
 
+class ConsentRequired(OdiError):
+    """The agent tried to act on the workspace before the PM agreed to it."""
+
+
 class StoreError(OdiError):
     """The persistence layer could not complete the operation."""
 
 
 class SerializationError(OdiError):
     """A payload could not be converted to or from its wire format."""
 
 
 _STATUS_BY_ERROR: tuple[tuple[type[OdiError], int], ...] = (
     (ValidationError, 400),
     (NotFoundError, 404),
     (ConflictError, 409),
     (RateLimitError, 429),
+    (ConsentRequired, 403),
     (StoreError, 500),
     (SerializationError, 502),
 )
 
 
 def error_status(err: OdiError) -> int:
     """Map an ODI error onto the HTTP status code that best describes it.
 
     Unknown :class:`OdiError` subclasses fall back to ``500`` rather than
     raising, so a new error type can never break an error handler.
     """
     for error_type, status in _STATUS_BY_ERROR:
         if isinstance(err, error_type):
             return status
     return 500

+"""Shared error model and parser for MCP tool results."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+
+class StudioErrorCode(str, Enum):
+    MCP_UNREACHABLE = "mcp_unreachable"
+    MCP_TOOL_FAILED = "mcp_tool_failed"
+    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
+    LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED = "llm_tool_rounds_exhausted"
+    NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
+    VALIDATION = "validation"
+    OUT_OF_RANGE = "out_of_range"
+    CONFLICT = "conflict"
+    INTERNAL = "internal"
+
+
+class StudioError(BaseModel):
+    code: StudioErrorCode
+    message: str
+    detail: str | None = None
+    suggestion: str | None = None
+    retryable: bool = False
+    request_id: str | None = None
+
+
+_OUT_OF_RANGE_MARKERS = (
+    "must be between",
+    "out of range",
+    "must be greater than",
+    "must be less than",
+)
+_VALIDATION_MARKERS = (
+    "is required",
+    "must not be empty",
+    "invalid ",
+)
+
+
+def parse_tool_result(text: str) -> StudioError | None:
+    """Return a classified error for an MCP error string, or ``None`` on success."""
+    if not text:
+        return None
+
+    stripped = text.strip()
+    lowered = stripped.lower()
+    is_error = lowered.startswith("error:") or " not found:" in lowered
+    if not is_error:
+        return None
+
+    message = stripped
+    if lowered.startswith("error:"):
+        message = stripped[len("error:") :].strip()
+
+    lowered_message = message.lower()
+    if "not found" in lowered_message:
+        return StudioError(
+            code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
+            message=message,
+            suggestion="Check the identifier and try again.",
+        )
+    if "unreachable" in lowered_message or "connection refused" in lowered_message:
+        return StudioError(
+            code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
+            message=message,
+            suggestion="Check that the MCP server is running, then retry.",
+            retryable=True,
+        )
+    if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _OUT_OF_RANGE_MARKERS):
+        return StudioError(
+            code=StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE,
+            message=message,
+            suggestion="Use a value inside the documented range.",
+        )
+    if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _VALIDATION_MARKERS):
+        return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION, message=message)
+
+    return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED, message=message)
+
+
+def tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
+    """Extract readable text from a FastMCP ``CallToolResult`` or a plain value."""
+    if isinstance(result, str):
+        return result
+
+    content = getattr(result, "content", None)
+    if content:
+        first = content[0]
+        text = getattr(first, "text", None)
+        if text is not None:
+            return str(text)
+
+    return str(result)

--- packages/core/tests/test_consent_pause.py	
+++ packages/core/tests/test_consent_pause.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+"""The agent must not act on the workspace before the PM agrees."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_core.consent import ACTING_TOOLS, READ_ONLY_TOOLS, ConsentGate
+from agentic_odi_core.contract import ToolName
+from agentic_odi_core.errors import ConsentRequired
+from agentic_odi_core.models import Job
+from agentic_odi_core.repository import InMemoryRepository
+
+
+def _repo_with_job() -> InMemoryRepository:
+    repo = InMemoryRepository()
+    repo.add_job(Job(id="job-1", name="Onboard customers"))
+    return repo
+
+
+def test_an_acting_call_mutates_nothing_until_consent() -> None:
+    repo = _repo_with_job()
+    gate = ConsentGate()
+    proposal = gate.request(ToolName.DELETE_JOB.value, {"job_id": "job-1"})
+
+    def delete(arguments):
+        return repo.delete_job(arguments["job_id"])
+
+    with pytest.raises(ConsentRequired):
+        gate.execute(proposal, delete)
+    assert repo.get_job("job-1") is not None
+
+    gate.approve(proposal)
+    assert gate.execute(proposal, delete) is True
+    assert repo.get_job("job-1") is None
+
+
+def test_a_declined_proposal_never_runs() -> None:
+    repo = _repo_with_job()
+    gate = ConsentGate()
+    proposal = gate.request(ToolName.DELETE_JOB.value, {"job_id": "job-1"})
+
+    assert gate.decline(proposal) is True
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        gate.execute(proposal, lambda arguments: repo.delete_job(arguments["job_id"]))
+    assert repo.get_job("job-1") is not None
+
+
+def test_an_approval_runs_only_once() -> None:
+    gate = ConsentGate()
+    proposal = gate.request(ToolName.ADD_JOB.value, {"name": "Onboard customers"})
+    gate.approve(proposal)
+
+    gate.execute(proposal, lambda arguments: arguments["name"])
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        gate.execute(proposal, lambda arguments: arguments["name"])
+
+
+def test_read_only_tools_do_not_need_consent() -> None:
+    gate = ConsentGate()
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        gate.request(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value)
+
+

 """Protected files must never be deleted on main.
 
 A deletion of a protected file breaks GitHub Pages deployment or the site
 contract. CI must fail red instead of staying green.
 
 The test reads ``.ci/protected-files.txt`` and compares the current tree
 against the base commit (the merge-base with the default branch, or the
 previous commit on a direct push to main). If any protected file that
 exists on the base is missing now, the test fails.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import subprocess
 from pathlib import Path
 
-import pytest
-
 ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
 MANIFEST = ROOT / ".ci" / "protected-files.txt"
 
 
 def _protected_paths() -> list[Path]:
     paths: list[Path] = []
     for line in MANIFEST.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
         line = line.strip()
         if not line or line.startswith("#"):
             continue
         paths.append(ROOT / line)
     return paths
 
 
 def _base_ref() -> str:
     """The ref to diff against.
 
     On a pull request we diff against the merge-base with the default
     branch so we see what the branch changed. On a direct push to main we
     fall back to the previous commit.
     """
     for candidate in ("origin/main", "main"):
         try:
             base = subprocess.check_output(
                 ["git", "merge-base", candidate, "HEAD"],
                 text=True,
                 cwd=ROOT,
             ).strip()
             if base:
                 return base
         except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
             continue
     # Direct push to main with no fetchable default branch: compare to HEAD~1.
     return "HEAD~1"
 
 
 def _deleted_files(base: str) -> set[str]:
     """Files deleted between ``base`` and HEAD."""
     output = subprocess.check_output(
         ["git", "diff", "--name-status", base, "HEAD"],
         text=True,
         cwd=ROOT,
     )
     deleted: set[str] = set()
     for line in output.splitlines():
         status, _, path = line.partition("\t")
         if status == "D":
             deleted.add(path)
     return deleted
 
 
 def _git_revision_path(ref: str, path: Path) -> str:
     return str(path.relative_to(ROOT))
 
 
 def test_no_protected_file_is_deleted() -> None:
     base = _base_ref()
     deleted = _deleted_files(base)
     violations = []
     for path in _protected_paths():
         rel = _git_revision_path(base, path)
         if rel in deleted:
             violations.append(rel)
 
     assert not violations, (
         "Protected files must not be deleted: "
         + ", ".join(sorted(violations))
         + f"\nBase ref: {base}"
     )

CLI Reference

Backends, chat, entities, and scoring.

The agentic-odi CLI is a Typer-based command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data commands are local-first: they read and write a SQLite store with no server required, and switch to a remote MCP server with --backend mcp.

Install the workspace first if you have not already:

uv sync --all-packages

Launching

python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
 python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
 python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)

A console script is also installed, so agentic-odi --version works the same way.

Global options

Option Environment variable Default Meaning
--backend local|mcp AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND local Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server.
--db PATH AGENTIC_ODI_DB ~/.agentic-odi/odi.db Store path for the local backend.
--mcp-url URL AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL http://localhost:8000/mcp Server URL for the mcp backend.

Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add --json for machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero (0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error).

Interactive chat

agentic-odi chat (or simply agentic-odi in a terminal) starts an offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service, and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.

agentic-odi chat
 agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp

Connection settings

The chat resolves settings in priority order: CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.

Variable Default CLI flag
AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL http://localhost:8001/v1 --base-url
AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL local-tools-model --model
AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY local --api-key
AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL http://localhost:8000/mcp --mcp-url

The persisted profile is stored at ~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json. You can create or update it from within the session using /connect.

Slash commands

Command Description
/help Show all available commands
/status Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status
/connect Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save
/model <name> Hot-swap to a different model mid-session
/mcp <url> Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session
/tools List the MCP tools the assistant can call
/clear Reset conversation history (keeps connection)
/exit Quit the session (also /quit)

/connect wizard

/connect walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:

  1. Provider — choose openai, anthropic, local, or other
  2. Base URL — preset filled for known providers; override freely
  3. API key — input is hidden via getpass
  4. Model — sensible default per provider
  5. MCP URL — defaults to the current value
  6. Save to profile? — writes ~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json so settings persist across sessions

The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.

[!NOTE] Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The customer-outcomes and connectors commands keep working without one.

Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes

Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a Job cascades to both.

# Jobs
 agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
 agentic-odi jobs list
 agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
 agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
 agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
 
 # Steps (Job Map)
 agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
 agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
 agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
 agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
 
 # Desired Outcomes
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

Add --json to any command for machine-readable output.

Evidence

Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.

# Capture a record by hand
 agentic-odi evidence add \
   --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
   --name "Support lead" \
   --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
   --job-id <job-id>
 
 # Read and delete
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
 agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
 agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
 
 # Promote into the ODI model
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>

connectors ingest --job-id <job-id> maps every evidence-bearing record in the ingested batch into evidence in one step.

Schema and scoring

-
agentic-odi schema                   # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
-agentic-odi framework-guidelines     # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide
-agentic-odi capabilities             # what the assistant can help with
-agentic-odi score 8 2                # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+
agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
 
Manage Customer Outcomes

 
Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The local backend
 writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add --backend mcp
 to route through a running MCP server (python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server). The group is also
 available under its historical name outcomes.

 
# Add a Customer Outcome
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
   --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
 
 # Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
   --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
 
 # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
 
 # Get, update, delete
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 
 # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
 agentic-odi score 8 2
 agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
 
score applies the ODI opportunity formula,
 importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0).

 
Set AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL (or --mcp-url) to point to a non-default server when
 using --backend mcp (default: http://localhost:8000/mcp).

 
Connectors

 
The connectors group manages external MCP integrations. See
 External Connectors for presets, the connector registry, and
 ingest behavior.

 
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
 
Updates

 
odi update checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
 default; disable it with --no-update for one run or
 AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1 globally. See Installation.

Roadmap & Next Steps

What has shipped, and what is queued.

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

  • [x] External MCP client connector: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
  • [x] Conversational rich surfaces: the studio agent composes validated cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them in prose.
  • [x] Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store.
  • [x] First-run wizard: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context conversation — isolated in apps/studio/src/onboarding/ behind the firstRunWizard flag.
  • [x] Additional connector kinds: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same Connector protocol.
  • [x] ODI Schema Definition: Define standardized Pydantic models for Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes.
  • [x] CLI Dataset Commands: Extend apps/cli so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
  • [x] Context Tooling: Replace the dummy greet tool with capabilities like get_job_map(job_id), get_outcomes(job_id), get_step(step_id), get_outcome(outcome_id), or evaluate_outcome(statement).
  • [x] Data Persistence Layer: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
  • [x] Agentic Integration: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the openai package) so the LLM can discover the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.
